links.targetTitle: The 90% Encumbrance Ratio cap is a commitment by Grove Devel

title: Keel gives a hard covenant to stay at or below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.3.1 is one sentence long and does a great deal: "Keel will operate the Keel Liquidity Layer and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio," referring to the Core Atlas definition at A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1.

The framing as an *agreement* rather than a parameter is what makes it enforceable in the way the rest of the section needs. The Freezer Multisig's usage standard authorizes a freeze when "Keel is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management" — a standard that requires a bright line to be actionable. The 90% covenant supplies it: compliance is checkable, and a breach is a named condition rather than a judgment call about prudence.

Defining the ratio upstream in the Risk Capital article rather than in Keel's Artifact matters too. Keel cannot redefine the metric it is measured by through a Root Edit, so tokenholders can vote on strategy but not on the arithmetic of their own leverage limit.

The residual 10% margin is the interesting judgment. It concedes that an Agent operating at nearly full encumbrance is acceptable, which is a high-utilization stance — the buffer against adverse moves is thin by design, and the compensating controls are the rate limits, the debt ceiling buffer parameter, and a freeze that can be pulled by two external signers.
description: The commitment is stated as part of Keel's agreement to operate the Liquidity Layer and refers to the Core Atlas definition, making leverage a bounded promise rather than an operational preference.
